name: Live-rig e2e after a team.rego/projection change: restart OPA + rebuild the usermgmt image + recreate the pod, then grep the e2e for OLD-contract cells
description: Running the e2e after a 6.7-style control-plane change needs THREE rig steps, in order: (1) restart OPA (docker restart opa-abac-opa) so it reloads the edited team.rego + permission_categories.json from the ./opa/policies mount (--watch unreliable) — verify with curl localhost:28181/v1/data/permission_categories + opa eval probes; (2) rebuild the usermgmt image with the NEW Java (docker build -q -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . — a full Gradle-in-container build, slow); (3) recreate the pod: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate usermgmt, then wait for localhost:28090/actuator/health. The CATALOG image does NOT need rebuilding (no catalog code changed; catalog cells decide via the shared OPA). Intended-break sweep: the existing e2e matrices encode the OLD contract — team-abac cell 8 ('viewer GET /members -> 403') and the permission-categories cells assert pre-6.7 outcomes; the list-members loosening flips viewer/member GET /members to 200, so REWRITE those cells (viewer lists 200 / mutates 403) and ADD explicit loosening cells. Add new cells via a Python json edit reusing the runner's existing --env-var tokens (senior_token/ladder_token/team_id/target1_uid). Result: permission-categories 31/31, team 12/12, all other matrices unaffected (list-members inert on catalog) -> 129 assertions across 10 matrices, 0 failed.

name: Trace the APISIX->OPA->app->DB chain into Jaeger locally
description: Phase B of the example rig adds end-to-end distributed tracing. Pattern that worked: (1) Jaeger v2 + embedded Badger (jaegertracing/jaeger:2.17.0, --config=jaeger-config.yaml) for persistent traces with no JVM (avoids aarch64 SIGILL of ES/OpenSearch). (2) APISIX opentelemetry plugin via plugin_attr.opentelemetry.collector.address=jaeger:4318, enabled per-route with {"opentelemetry":{"sampler":{"name":"always_on"}}}. (3) OTEL Java agent BAKED INTO the app image (ADD opentelemetry-javaagent.jar /opt/otel/agent.jar) and attached per-pod via -javaagent + OTEL_SERVICE_NAME/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://opa-abac-jaeger:4318/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf. (4) OPA with distributed_tracing.type=grpc,address=jaeger:4317 emits its own decision spans. Verified: GET /api/services returns [apisix, catalog-management-service, opa, jaeger]; one APISIX trace nests gateway->app->JPA/DB spans. Note: APISIX opa plugin does NOT propagate trace context into the OPA call, so OPA spans are a separate service, not nested — expected. All host ports for Jaeger(16686/4317/4318)/OPA(8181) clash with a running portal podman-machine, so remap host side to 2xxxx; in-network DNS (opa-abac-jaeger:4318, opa:8181) is unaffected.

Two docker-rig operational gotchas surfaced during the 2026-07-12 rig rebuild. (1) HOST-PORT / RUNTIME COLLISION: the machine runs the starter rig on DOCKER and a separate unrelated project (IdP/portal) on PODMAN simultaneously. The podman stack binds the CANONICAL ports (opa-standalone :8181, keycloak-abac :8888, apisix :9080, portal-postgres :5432) while the docker starter rig is remapped to +20000-style host ports (opa-abac-opa :28181, opa-abac-keycloak :28888, apisix :9085->9080). Any localhost probe of the starter OPA MUST use :28181, NOT :8181 — hitting :8181 lands on the podman OPA (a paas/projects bundle) and every data.catalog.* returns undefined. This caused a false 'wrong bundle mounted' finding in the 7.4 security review. Verify which OPA you are talking to with: curl -s localhost:28181/v1/policies | grep catalog. (2) deploy.sh build EXIT-CODE MASKING: a docker build that FAILS (e.g. the ADD https://github.com/.../opentelemetry-javaagent.jar step dying with 'unexpected EOF' under a flaky network) still let ./deploy.sh build report exit 0 in one observed run — the wrapper did not propagate the buildkit failure. Always check the tail of the build output for 'ERROR: failed to build' / 'RC=1', do not trust the deploy.sh exit code alone. Separately, docker's ADD <github-release-url> is itself flaky (redirect-to-CDN cache-key fetch); DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 did not help when Docker Hub base-layer pulls were ALSO failing (transient registry outage). When images are unchanged vs the tree, skip the rebuild entirely and deploy.sh up on the existing :local images.
resolution: RIG PROBE PORTS (docker starter, when podman IdP stack co-runs): OPA localhost:28181, Keycloak localhost:28888, gateway localhost:9085. In-network token mint still uses the compose network (docker run --network opa-abac-example_default -> keycloak:8888 INSIDE the docker net — that 8888 is the container port, unaffected by the host remap). Base infra ordering: ./deploy.sh down tears down base Postgres too, so a subsequent ./deploy.sh up errors 'Postgres not running' — run ./profile.sh up FIRST, then ./deploy.sh up --pods N. Rebuild only when app SOURCE changed since the :local image timestamp (git log --since=<image age> -- example-*/src); the catalog.rego / OPA policies are bind-mounted from disk (NOT baked into the app image), so a policy fix needs only an OPA container restart / rig up, never an app image rebuild.

description: ENABLE_OPA=0 is NOT a pure pod-env flip: deploy.sh passes ENABLE_OPA through to infra/apisix/init-routes.sh, which then OMITS the gateway's coarse allow-all opa plugin from the catalog-all route — so a naive two-pass guarded/baseline comparison conflates the gateway OPA hop with the app-side library gate. Also, opa.abac.enabled=false removes the starter's ENTIRE auto-config (class-level @ConditionalOnProperty), and until PR #61 the example apps had never booted that way (empty FilterRegistrationBean crashes Tomcat even disabled — getDescription() asserts; no AbacFilter = 401 wall on authenticated(); 4 components hard-injected starter beans).
resolution: For an identical-gateway baseline: after the ENABLE_OPA=0 deploy, re-run init-routes.sh with ENABLE_OPA=1 (the OPA container keeps running — deploy.sh up never stops it), and ASSERT the route posture per pass via the APISIX admin API (openid-connect + opa present on catalog-all). App-side: PR #61 gives the examples an honest unguarded profile (property-gated filter registration, gateway-trust chain, lazy starter-bean injection with fail-closed floors, UnguardedBootIT on real Tomcat). Lesson for planning: an ADR that pins a rig mechanism must include a 5-minute boot spike of that mechanism.

name: APISIX gateway plugin ordering for auth chain (oidc->enrich->opa)
description: On an APISIX route that does OIDC + identity enrichment + OPA, plugin execution order matters and is controlled by _meta.priority (HIGHER runs first), not by JSON key order. Proven chain (matches portal): openid-connect(2599) -> serverless-pre-function enricher(2500) -> opa(2000) = authenticate, then inject identity headers from the validated JWT, then authorize. WITHOUT an explicit override, serverless-pre-function defaults to a very high priority and would run BEFORE openid-connect (no validated token yet) — so you MUST pin its _meta.priority below openid-connect. The enricher is a small Lua that base64url-decodes the JWT payload (already verified by openid-connect; it only READS claims) and sets X-User-Id (sub) / X-Username (preferred_username) via core.request.set_header. Build the Lua-in-JSON via a Python helper (json.dumps) to avoid bash escaping bugs. Keycloak omits 'sub' from the access token unless you add an oidc-sub-mapper protocolMapper to the client in the realm export (access.token.claim=true).

content: The example rig (Docker) is designed to run SIMULTANEOUSLY with the maintainer's proprietary portal stack (podman-machine) — do NOT stop podman. They coexist because the rig deliberately publishes every host port in a SHIFTED range so nothing collides with the podman portal: gateway 9085 (not 9080), catalog pods 28081/28082 (BASE_PORT 28080, not the portal 18080 range), OPA 28181 (not 8181), Keycloak 28888 (not 8888), Jaeger 26686/24317/24318, Postgres 5433 (not 5432); APISIX admin 9180. In-network DNS (opa:8181, keycloak:8888, opa-abac-jaeger:4318) is unaffected by the host remap. Both engines coexist as separate VMs/daemons; the ONLY shared constraint is host ports (resolved by the shift) and machine RAM/CPU (lever is --pods, not engine interference). OPERATIONAL ORDERING GOTCHA: deploy.sh does NOT start the base Postgres — it asserts 'opa-abac-postgres' already exists and ERRORS with 'Postgres not running. Start base infra first: ./profile.sh up' otherwise. So the correct bring-up is: (1) ./profile.sh up (base Postgres on 5433, healthy), then (2) [ENABLE_OIDC=1] ./deploy.sh up --pods N (Jaeger/OPA/Keycloak/APISIX/etcd + N catalog pods; OIDC is OFF by default — set ENABLE_OIDC=1 to exercise Keycloak token minting + gateway auth; OPA + tracing are on by default). Expected-correct signals: GET :9085/actuator/health returns 302 (APISIX openid-connect redirecting to Keycloak — that's auth working, NOT a failure) — verify the app itself via a direct pod hit :28081/actuator/health => {status:UP}. The 'Found orphan containers [opa-abac-postgres]' compose warnings are harmless (Postgres belongs to the profile.sh project, the rest to the deploy.sh project).

description: Phase 5.9 e2e: the tag and team newman matrices failed on user-service endpoints (a define-tag 201 had no Location; a gated 403 returned application/json not application/problem+json) even after running ./deploy.sh build and redeploying. Root cause: ./deploy.sh build rebuilds ONLY the catalog app image (build_image). The user-management image (opa-abac-usermgmt:local) is rebuilt ONLY by build_usermgmt_image, which deploy.sh invokes lazily as 'usermgmt_image_exists || build_usermgmt_image' inside the up path — so when a stale usermgmt image already exists, NEITHER deploy.sh build NOR deploy.sh up rebuilds it. The pod therefore kept serving 6-day-old code (the legacy ApiError body, no Location). Catalog-side assertions passed because the catalog image WAS rebuilt; only the user-service-routed requests failed.
resolution: When a slice changes user-service code, force its image explicitly: docker build -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . (build context is the repo ROOT for the multi-module Gradle build), then recreate the container: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate, and wait for http://localhost:28090/actuator/health UP. Symptom signature: in a two-service e2e, contract assertions pass on catalog routes but fail on user-service routes with the OLD body shape -> suspect a stale usermgmt image, not a code bug. (Consider teaching deploy.sh build to also rebuild usermgmt when ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1.)

description: Local APISIX container-pool rig (deploy.sh) failed to start in several non-obvious ways: (1) APISIX 3.x reads etcd config under deployment.etcd, not a top-level 'etcd:' key — a top-level key is silently ignored, APISIX falls back to 127.0.0.1:2379, logs 'all etcd nodes are unavailable', and the container exits. (2) bitnami/etcd images are gone (Bitnami sunset their free Docker Hub catalog) -> 'manifest unknown'. (3) Host port clashes with a running portal podman-machine gvproxy: :9080 and the 18081/18082 range are already bound. (4) Killing Postgres mid-session (e.g. compose down --remove-orphans on one of the shared-project compose files) makes pods return 503 with java.net.UnknownHostException: opa-abac-postgres.
resolution: (1) Put etcd under deployment.etcd in apisix/config.yaml. (2) Use quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.x with explicit --listen-client-urls/--advertise-client-urls. (3) Use proxy port 9085 and pod base port 28080 (pods 28081+) to dodge the podman-machine. (4) All three composes share name: opa-abac-example so they share opa-abac-example_default; never run 'compose down --remove-orphans' on a single file — it deletes the others' containers. Pods auto-recover (HikariCP reconnect) within seconds once Postgres is back. Bonus: enable response-rewrite plugin and set X-Upstream-Addr=$upstream_addr on the route to prove round-robin.

description: SYMPTOM: 'ENABLE_SPA=1 ./deploy.sh up' aborts at require_postgres ('Postgres not running') even though ./profile.sh up already ran. ROOT CAUSE: profile.sh up ran while podman was the active runtime, so opa-abac-postgres landed on the podman machine (gvproxy holds host :5433); after switching to Docker Desktop, deploy.sh's 'docker ps | grep opa-abac-postgres' queries Docker Desktop and can't see the podman-side container. Compounding: the image build (plain 'docker build', no --builder) auto-selected the 'podman' buildx docker-container builder (log line: buildx_buildkit_podman), which would NOT load the image into Docker Desktop's store, so even a 'successful' build leaves docker compose unable to find opa-abac-catalog:local.
resolution: Pick ONE daemon and converge everything on it. (1) podman rm -f opa-abac-postgres to free :5433 from gvproxy; (2) docker buildx use desktop-linux (native docker driver -> loads images into the daemon store; the docker-container drivers do not without --load); (3) restart base infra on Docker Desktop (default context IS desktop-linux -> leave DOCKER_HOST unset); (4) re-run deploy.sh up. PREVENT: keep one runtime live; if switching runtimes mid-session, tear down the stranded stack first (host ports are held by gvproxy until the podman container is removed). Verified after: scripts/postman/run-spa-auth-smoke.sh -> 4/4 (no-token 401, invalid 401, valid 200 health + 200 read /api/v1/catalogs).

description: Keycloak realm-export import died at container start with 'Value too long for column DESCRIPTION CHARACTER VARYING(255)' — a client 'description' field in realm-export.json over 255 chars aborts the ENTIRE realm import (dev-mode H2 and real DBs share the column size), so Keycloak starts with NO realm and every dependent service 401s. The compose healthcheck (TCP on 8888) does NOT catch it — the port never opens, but the failure mode reads as 'keycloak slow to start'.
resolution: Keep realm-export.json description fields under 255 chars (move rationale to a JSON-adjacent doc or the ADR); after editing the export, docker compose up -d --force-recreate keycloak (dev-mode, no volume -> re-import) and grep the logs for 'Import finished successfully' before trusting the rig.

description: Wiring APISIX openid-connect to a Keycloak container hit two non-obvious failures: (1) 'unknown plugin [openid-connect]' on the route PUT — APISIX only loads plugins listed in config.yaml's top-level 'plugins:'; adding openid-connect there requires RECREATING the apisix container (editing the file isn't enough, and curl -sf swallows the 400 so the route silently lacks the plugin). (2) Keycloak issuer mismatch: Keycloak is hostname-aware, so the discovery doc + token issuer differ by how it's reached — in-network http://keycloak:8888 vs host http://localhost:28888. APISIX discovers + validates IN-NETWORK (issuer keycloak:8888), so a token minted against localhost:28888 has a mismatched issuer and is rejected. Tokens must be minted in-network or via the browser redirect flow.
resolution: (1) After changing config.yaml plugins, force-recreate apisix (docker compose up -d --force-recreate apisix) before seeding routes; don't trust curl -sf (drop -f or inspect the body). (2) Pin KC_HOSTNAME_URL=http://keycloak:8888 + KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false so the in-network issuer is stable; for testing, mint tokens in-network via 'docker run --network opa-abac-example_default curlimages/curl ... http://keycloak:8888/realms/catalog-demo/protocol/openid-connect/token'. Verified: no-token->302, valid in-network token->200, bad->401. ENABLE_OIDC gate keeps it opt-in. Service does NO JWT check (gateway-only auth, Phase 2).

description: Testcontainers ITs failed with 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' even though podman machine reported running. Root cause: the podman machine claimed State=running but its API socket file (ConnectionInfo.PodmanSocket.Path under TMPDIR) was MISSING (stale machine state), so the build's resolveDockerHost() (which checks file(path).exists()) returned null and Testcontainers fell back to default strategies that probe /var/run/docker.sock (a dead symlink to the absent podman sock) and the Docker Desktop CLI socket (not a usable API socket) — both fail. Exporting DOCKER_HOST in the shell does NOT help because the Gradle test worker fork does not inherit it and the build only injects DOCKER_HOST when resolveDockerHost() is non-null. ~/.testcontainers.properties docker.host was also not honored by the failing strategy order.
resolution: Restart the podman machine: podman machine stop then podman machine start. This recreates the API socket (start prints 'API forwarding listening on: /var/run/docker.sock'). Then resolveDockerHost() finds the socket via podman machine inspect and the build auto-injects DOCKER_HOST into the test task as designed. Environment fix, no code change. If podman is genuinely unavailable, point DOCKER_HOST at the Docker Desktop RAW socket (~/.docker/run/docker.sock, NOT the docker-cli.sock) so the build's priority-1 env branch fires.

title: Gateway-side identity/enrichment is demo scaffold; the library does real extraction
rationale: The example rig's gateway does OIDC termination (APISIX openid-connect) and a Lua serverless-pre-function that decodes the JWT and injects X-User-Id/X-Username for OPA. This gateway-side identity handling is DELIBERATELY a throwaway demo so the topology is visible/traceable end-to-end NOW, before the library exists. It is NOT the target architecture. The project thesis (POC-ROADMAP) is to be Spring-NATIVE with no gateway 'mediator': real subject/attribute extraction belongs in the library — opa-abac-spring-security's pluggable Authentication->AbacContext extractor (see mx-ea7974), feeding OpaAuthorizationManager / @OpaPreAuthorize, with the service doing its own fine-grained ABAC (two-layer model mx-7130a1). So in Phase 3 the demo Lua enricher gets removed; the app validates the JWT and extracts AbacContext itself. Keep the gateway doing only coarse auth (authn + a coarse OPA route check); push fine-grained, attribute-level decisions into the app via the library. Don't let the demo enricher calcify into the design.

description: Liquibase sql changesets that use Postgres jsonb operators containing '?' (jsonb_exists ?, ?| , ?&) fail at migration time with 'syntax error at or near $1' - the JDBC driver rewrites every ? as a bind-parameter placeholder before Postgres sees it. Surfaced in the 6.5 seed-sweep changeset (0006-permission-categories.yaml) where 'e.value ? ''read''' broke every Testcontainers IT boot.
resolution: Use the function forms instead of the operators in any SQL that flows through JDBC/Liquibase: jsonb_exists(col, 'key') for ?, jsonb_exists_any for ?|, jsonb_exists_all for ?&. Same semantics, no placeholder collision.

name: Adding a gateway-fronted service to the rig: the four steps, and the one everyone forgets
description:
ENABLE_MCP=1 (AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ T6) followed the ENABLE_SPA/ENABLE_DIRECTORY precedent: (1) infra/compose.<svc>.yaml on the shared opa-abac-example network + a Dockerfile; (2) deploy.sh — the flag force-enabling its prerequisites, <svc>_compose()/build_<svc>_image()/wait_<svc>_healthy(), up + down + status line; (3) pass the flag through to init-routes.sh; (4) THE FORGOTTEN ONE — infra/apisix/init-routes.sh needs an upstream + route. The catalog-all route is uri:/* at the APISIX DEFAULT priority 0, so it silently swallows any new path: without a route, POST /mcp is proxied to the catalog pool and 404s there, which reads as 'the new service is broken'. Priority ladder in use: catalog-all 0 < keycloak-proxy 50 < usermgmt 60 < mcp 65 < internal-blocked 70. Plugin set for an app that authorizes ITSELF = the usermgmt set (openid-connect + response-rewrite + tracing/cors), explicitly NOT the catalog An open source project to policy-enable your service.

Usage:
  opa [command]

Available Commands:
  bench        Benchmark a Rego query
  build        Build an OPA bundle
  capabilities Print the capabilities of OPA
  check        Check Rego source files
  completion   Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  deps         Analyze Rego query dependencies
  eval         Evaluate a Rego query
  exec         Execute against input files
  fmt          Format Rego source files
  help         Help about any command
  inspect      Inspect OPA bundle(s)
  parse        Parse Rego source file
  run          Start OPA in interactive or server mode
  sign         Generate an OPA bundle signature
  test         Execute Rego test cases
  version      Print the version of OPA

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for opa

Use "opa [command] --help" for more information about a command. gateway plugin. Also: every outbound base-URL must be overridden in-network — the shipped defaults are localhost, which in a pod is the pod; the ROLE-SOURCE url is the trap, since a wrong value denies every call with a policy-shaped error code. Keycloak protocol mappers that must yield a JSON array need jsonType.label=JSON with claim.value='["x"]'; jsonType.label=String mints a bare string, and a fail-closed extractor will correctly but confusingly deny it.

SYMPTOM: an e2e drill that needs a service reconfigured mid-suite (kill-switch off, capability revoked) recreates the pod with 'VAR=value docker compose -f infra/compose.<svc>.yaml up -d --force-recreate <svc>' - and the override silently does nothing, or an explicitly EMPTY override falls back to the default.
resolution: Two separate causes. (1) The compose file must INTERPOLATE the value; a literal 'KEY: "value"' ignores the environment. (2) Use the BARE-DASH default form ${VAR-default}, not ${VAR:-default}: the colon form treats set-but-empty as unset, so 'MCP_READONLY_TOOLS= docker compose up -d' would restore the default profile instead of revoking it - and a revocation drill that silently does not revoke PASSES for the wrong reason if the assertion is 'denied'. AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ T6 uses this for both the two kill-switches and the readonly actor's four capability dimensions. Always pair the recreate with a health WAIT on the pod (poll actuator/health for '"status":"UP"') before the folder that depends on the new switch, and put an EXIT trap in the runner that restores the default profile - a failed drill otherwise leaves the rig switched off for the next run.

description: P0 PROBE for the supervisor/step-up slice (2026-08-01): does auth_time reach the ACCESS token on this rig's Keycloak? FIRST DATAPOINT, ROPC path: NO — a password-grant token from catalog-gateway carries sid/iat/exp/scope/realm_access but auth_time, acr AND amr are all ABSENT. Full claim set: azp, email, email_verified, exp, family_name, given_name, iat, iss, jti, name, preferred_username, realm_access, scope, sid, sub, typ. NOT CONCLUSIVE for the question as asked: ROPC is a non-interactive grant, so auth_time/acr/amr may legitimately be omitted there while still being present on the authorization-code flow the demo SPA uses (PKCE). The definitive probe is a BROWSER login through the SPA, decoding the access token Keycloak returns to the code flow.
resolution: TWO separate consequences, and the second is the one that changes the decomposition. (1) Still run the code-flow probe before decompose — drive the SPA's PKCE login (the Browser pane can) and decode the resulting ACCESS token, not the ID token; the KC #31572 regression is specifically about access tokens, and refresh preserves acr for the whole session ('refresh laundering'), so RS-side auth_time freshness is THE control. (2) REGARDLESS of that answer: EVERY token-minting path in this repo is grant_type=password — all 15 postman runners, the agent matrix, seed-demo-data.sh — and ROPC structurally cannot carry auth_time. So a step-up slice cannot be e2e-tested through the existing harness at all: it needs a NEW token-acquisition path (code flow, or a Keycloak protocol-mapper/hardcoded-claim shim for the test identities) as an explicit DELIVERABLE, not an implementation detail discovered mid-run. Pin it in the decomposition's ticket list, the same way the AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ package had to pin the APISIX route the e2e needed.

description: P0 step-up precondition: auth_time/acr/amr were ABSENT from every token the rig mints (both the ROPC gateway grant AND the SPA authorization-code+PKCE flow), which looked like the KC #31572 access-token regression. It is NOT that regression. Root cause is self-inflicted realm config: infra/keycloak/realm-export.json pins each client's defaultClientScopes to the literal list [openid, profile, email, roles]. 'openid' is not a client scope (silently ignored), and the explicit list REPLACES Keycloak's built-in default assignment - so the built-in 'basic' scope (which since KC 25 carries the auth_time oidc-usersessionmodel-note-mapper, access.token.claim=true) and the 'acr' scope (oidc-acr-mapper) end up assigned to NO client in the realm, though both exist. Measured on the rig 2026-08-01, Keycloak 26.3.2.
resolution: Assign the built-in 'basic' and 'acr' client scopes as DEFAULT scopes on the clients (admin API PUT /clients/{id}/default-client-scopes/{scopeId}); in realm-export.json either drop the explicit defaultClientScopes list or extend it to include basic + acr. VERIFIED after assignment: authorization-code+PKCE access token carries auth_time=<login time> and acr, with iat advancing independently (auth_time 1785567310 vs iat 1785567409). REFRESH-LAUNDERING CONFIRMED: refreshing preserves BOTH auth_time and acr while iat advances - so RS-side (now - auth_time) freshness is the only control that survives refresh, exactly as the design assumed. ROPC SPLIT CONFIRMED: with 'basic' assigned, the password grant still yields NO auth_time (the mapper reads the AUTH_TIME user-session note, which direct-grant never sets) but DOES yield acr=1, while an SSO-reused browser session yields acr=0 - so acr alone is not a control and a non-ROPC token-acquisition path remains a ticket-level e2e deliverable. Rig capability pins (26.3.2, vs the brief's assumed 26.7.0): auth-otp-form, webauthn-authenticator, webauthn-authenticator-passwordless (passkey), auth-recovery-authn-code-form, conditional-level-of-authentication and oidc-amr-mapper ALL present - so no KC upgrade is needed for TOTP, the conditional-LoA subflow, the passkey swap demo, or amr. realm attribute acr.loa.map is UNSET (a realm-export deliverable) and amr is in no assigned scope (needs an explicit mapper).

description: TWO rig gotchas hit in one T6 e2e run (SUPERVISED-SCOPE, 2026-08-07). (1) OPA READINESS: a matrix runner that restarts the OPA container (mandatory after any policy edit - --watch does not reliably reload) must NOT poll /health to decide it is back. OPA answers /health as soon as the SERVER is listening, which is BEFORE the policy bundle is loaded, and a decision asked in that window returns undefined - which every fail-closed client in this repo reads as DENY. Symptom: the runner's own fixture creation through the gateway comes back 403 and the run aborts before newman even starts, looking exactly like an authorization bug in the code under test. It cost a full run. (2) DOCKER PULL WEDGED: docker's image-pull path can wedge on this machine while the registry is perfectly reachable - 'docker pull alpine' hangs indefinitely and a build fails at FROM with 'DeadlineExceeded: context deadline exceeded', yet curl to registry-1.docker.io returns 401 in 0.5s FROM THE HOST *and* from inside the Docker VM (docker run curlimages/curl). So 'the network is down' is the wrong diagnosis and waiting does not help.
resolution: (1) Poll a REAL DECISION, not /health: curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:28181/v1/data/catalog/allow -d '{"input":{}}' until the body carries a "result" key, then hard-fail after a bounded wait instead of proceeding into a misleading 403. (2) Use podman as a BUILD/TRANSPORT tool while keeping the rig on Docker: 'podman pull ' then 'podman save --format docker-archive | docker load' for the base images, and 'podman build -v "$HOME/.gradle:/root/.gradle" -t -f .' for the app images, then save/load into Docker and re-tag from localhost/ to . The gradle-cache MOUNT is the other half of the win and is worth doing even on a healthy Docker: the committed Dockerfiles run ./gradlew INSIDE the build stage, so every image build re-downloads the ~150MB gradle distribution plus all dependencies from services.gradle.org - measured >40 min and stalling, versus UNDER TWO MINUTES with the host cache mounted. Same committed Dockerfile, same source, same gradle version - only the build's inputs come from a local cache, exactly like a CI cache. This does NOT violate the portal=podman/opa-abac=Docker separation (mx-2c4a1a): nothing is RUN on podman, the rig containers are all still Docker's. Also worth copying: capture the WHOLE response body when a runner's fixture creation fails (a bare 'json_field id' pipe turns any non-201 into a Python KeyError and throws away the problem+json that names the cause - it immediately exposed a fixture payload using invented field names).

name: Packaged demo SPA: nginx sidecar + priority-40 static routes; ENABLE_SPA previously only set auth posture
description: Until 2026-08-12, ENABLE_SPA=1 configured ONLY the gateway posture (bearer-only + /realms//resources Keycloak passthrough + CORS) — the demo-ui README's 'packaged demo served through APISIX' claim was never implemented; the SPA worked solely via the Vite dev server on :3000, and the gateway root 401'd (bearer-only catch-all). The packaged mode now exists: (1) infra/compose.spa.yaml — nginx:alpine 'spa' container mounting example-demo-ui/dist read-only, NO published host port (reached only through the gateway), wget healthcheck; (2) infra/spa/default.conf — try_files fallback to index.html; (3) deploy.sh — build_spa_bundle() runs host-side npm ci+vite build (like the host Gradle wrapper: bundle is a build artifact, container only serves), spa_compose up/down gated on ENABLE_SPA; (4) init-routes.sh — upstream spa-static {spa:80} + routes spa-index (uris /, /index.html, /vite.svg, /favicon.ico) and spa-assets (/assets/*) at PRIORITY 40: above catalog-all (0), below keycloak proxy (50) and usermgmt prefixes (60), GET/HEAD only, no auth plugins (static bundle is public; every data call still bearer-gated — verified /api 401 after the change). Key discoveries: the realm client catalog-spa ALREADY had http://localhost:9085/* redirect+webOrigins (the packaged mode was designed for, just never wired); APISIX cannot serve static files natively, hence the nginx sidecar following the compose-per-feature precedent (mx-5ca765). Verified live: SPA at :9085 does full PKCE through the gateway-proxied Keycloak, all four personas walk correctly (editor owner-everything / demo edit-no-manage / viewer padlocked mutations / outsider empty list).

The packaged-SPA healthcheck could never pass on first implementation: busybox wget in nginx:alpine resolves localhost to ::1 first, and a MOUNTED custom conf listens IPv4-only — the stock image's 10-listen-on-ipv6-by-default.sh entrypoint patches ONLY its own default.conf (checksum-gated), never a mounted one. compose 'up -d' does not block on health, so the rig demo worked while the container sat permanently unhealthy — live verification of the ENDPOINTS masked the defect; only 'docker inspect <name> .State.Health' shows it. Found by the pre-PR adversarial review workflow (PR #102), confirmed on the live rig.
resolution: Probe the IPv4 loopback explicitly in the healthcheck (wget http://127.0.0.1/) AND add 'listen [::]:80;' beside 'listen 80;' in any mounted nginx conf. Always docker-inspect health state as part of verifying a new compose service — a working endpoint through the gateway proves nothing about the container's own healthcheck.

description: Flag-gated APISIX route blocks that only PUT on flag=1 leave STALE PUBLIC ROUTES after a flip-off re-up: the etcd container is reused across './deploy.sh up' runs (only 'down' removes it), and init-routes.sh had no DELETE arm anywhere — so a previous ENABLE_SPA=1 deploy's public routes at '/' (priority 40) kept shadowing the OIDC redirect posture of a later non-SPA rig, and the never-stopped sidecar kept serving the stale bundle. The same disease pre-exists for the keycloak-realms/keycloak-resources passthrough routes and the /mcp route (they linger when their flags flip off). Found by two independent lenses of the PR #102 review; confirmed E2E (flip-off left / serving the SPA instead of the 302).
resolution: Make flag-gated route blocks TWO-ARMED: else-arm DELETEs the routes THEN the upstream (APISIX refuses to drop an upstream a route still references; plain curl -s so a 404 is a no-op under set -e), and deploy.sh mirrors it with '<svc>_compose down' when the flag is off. PR #102 fixed the SPA block; PR #103 completed the pattern for the keycloak-realms/keycloak-resources routes (ROUTES ONLY — the container is shared with plain ENABLE_OIDC and survives) and the mcp route + container. The ENABLE_USER_SERVICE block stays one-armed DELIBERATELY (its containers survive flag-flips, so its routes stay live, not stale). Caveat in the matrix headers: flavour flags must be EXPORTED to survive another matrix's rig re-up, since flag-off arms now tear surfaces down.

name: P0 auth_time probe ANSWERED (KC 26.3.2): request-side dead, session-note mapper works, refresh preserves login time
description: The definitive slice-C probe, run 2026-08-13 on the live rig (quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3.2, realm catalog-demo, scripted PKCE code flow against catalog-spa — NOT ROPC). (1) DEFAULT: auth_time/acr/amr ABSENT from BOTH the access token and the ID token. (2) REQUEST-SIDE IS A DEAD END on this version: max_age=300 -> still absent (a spec deviation — OIDC Core requires auth_time in the ID token under max_age; the KC #31572 regression class is live); claims={id_token:{auth_time:{essential:true}}} -> absent; acr_values=1 -> absent. (3) THE MAPPER CONTINGENCY WORKS: oidc-usersessionmodel-note-mapper with user.session.note=AUTH_TIME, claim.name=auth_time, jsonType long, on the client -> the real login epoch lands in BOTH tokens (verified value == login wall-clock). (4) THE KEYSTONE for the RS-side freshness control: a refresh_token grant PRESERVES auth_time at the ORIGINAL login time (measured identical pre/post refresh) — refresh does NOT launder the authentication instant, so RS-side 'now - auth_time > threshold' genuinely forces re-auth regardless of refresh cadence. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE for STEP-UP-ELEVATION: the auth_time protocol mapper on the realm export is a REQUIRED slice-C deliverable (the realm diff B was forbidden is C's territory), and the e2e token path must be the scripted code flow (this probe's script shape: cookie-jar GET /auth -> POST login-actions form WITH the Secure-flagged cookies forced over http (requests refuses them silently — 'Restart login cookie not found' 400 is the tell) -> exchange with code_verifier). ROPC structurally cannot carry auth_time — every existing runner's mint_token() is unusable for step-up cells.

CORRECTION of mx-afd666's diagnosis (same measurements, wrong attribution). The 2026-08-13 probe's 'request-side is dead / KC #31572 regression class is live' framing is WRONG for this rig: ADR 0030 §Context had already diagnosed the root cause on 2026-08-01 — the realm export pins defaultClientScopes to the literal list [openid, profile, email, roles] on both clients and defines NO clientScopes, which REPLACES Keycloak's built-in scope assignment and leaves the built-in 'basic' scope (which carries the auth_time session-note mapper) and the 'acr' scope assigned to no client. Verified in infra/keycloak/realm-export.json 2026-08-13. The 08-13 probe measured the committed-export baseline because the rig re-imported the realm since the 08-01 live patch (slice A's personas forced down/up). The manual oidc-usersessionmodel-note-mapper probe validated the same mechanism 'basic' carries — it was a redundant contingency, not the required fix.
resolution: Slice C's realm deliverable is ADR 0030's fix: assign the built-in 'basic' + 'acr' client scopes in the realm export (restore default KC behavior), NOT a custom mapper. Still valid from mx-afd666: refresh PRESERVES auth_time (re-confirmed 08-13 — the RS-side freshness control is sound); the scripted PKCE code flow as the non-ROPC e2e token path, incl. the Secure-cookie-over-http 400 gotcha ('Restart login cookie not found' = requests silently withholding Secure cookies on plain http — force the Cookie header). LESSON: before recording a probe verdict, grep the ADRs for a prior diagnosis of the same symptom — the 08-01 half-probe's diagnosis was one grep away.

description: Keycloak 26.3.2 step-up realm: a LONE 'Condition - Level of Authentication' subflow at level 2 demands the second factor on EVERY fresh login, not only when the client requests acr_values=aal2. Read off the shipped class (javap -c on org.keycloak.keycloak-services-26.3.2.jar): ConditionalLoaAuthenticator.matchCondition logs "Condition '%s' evaluated to true due the user not yet reached any authentication level in this session, configuredLoa: %d, requestedLoa: %d" - the no-level-yet branch short-circuits BEFORE any requested-vs-configured comparison, so requestedLoa=-1 (nothing requested) still matches. Symptom during STEP-UP-ELEVATION T1: a plain scripted PKCE code flow got login.ftl then login-otp.ftl. Setting the realm attribute default.acr.values=["aal1"] does NOT help (same branch runs first). Second trap in the same class: LoAUtil.getMaxAgeFromLoaConditionConfiguration falls back to 0 when 'loa-max-age' is absent ('Invalid max age configured ... Fallback to 0'), i.e. the level is never remembered for future authentications - a level-1 condition without an explicit max age re-prompts for the password on every step-up.
resolution: Wrap the password in its OWN level-1 conditional subflow ahead of the level-2 one, and give BOTH conditions an explicit loa-max-age: forms -> [CONDITIONAL level-1: conditional-level-of-authentication(loa-condition-level=1, loa-max-age=36000) + auth-username-password-form] then [CONDITIONAL level-2: conditional-level-of-authentication(loa-condition-level=2, loa-max-age=300) + auth-otp-form], both members REQUIRED. An ordinary login then settles at LoA 1 (acr=aal1 via acr.loa.map) and level 2 fires only for clients that ask. 36000 is Keycloak's own legacy fallback constant for loa-store-in-user-session. Also drop the built-in conditional-user-configured 2FA subflow from a step-up browser flow: it prompts any user WITH a factor at every login while the LoA machinery still records level 1 - a factor that elevates nothing. THIRD finding, the useful one: a PARTIAL authenticationFlows block in a realm export does NOT suppress Keycloak's built-ins (26.3.2) - declaring only the custom flows still leaves browser/registration/direct grant/reset credentials/clients/docker auth/first broker login created and every other flow binding resolving, so a custom flow costs ~150 lines of export, not a ~700-line full flow dump.

description: STEP-UP e2e, KC 26.3.2: Keycloak enforces TOTP codes as ONE-TIME per credential. Two elevations inside the same 30s window fail on the re-rendered OTP form with a bare 'Invalid authenticator code.' - byte-identical to what a WRONG SECRET produces, so the misdiagnosis is 'my RFC 6238 computation is broken'. It is not an edge case for a step-up matrix: the round-trip cell, the freshness drill's positive control and the loop-prevention negative all elevate within a couple of minutes. Symptom in a scripted flow: the miner re-answers the SAME code (same window) and loops until it runs out of form steps, aborting with 'no authorization code after N steps'. Reproduced deliberately (two mints back to back, both submitting 571466; the first succeeded, every later submission of that code was rejected).
resolution: Detect the RE-RENDERED OTP form as the error signal (Keycloak answers a rejected code with the same form + an inline message at status 200, not a 4xx), remember the codes already submitted in this invocation, and when the freshly-computed code is one of them, SLEEP to the next period boundary (period - now%period + 1s) and recompute. Bound the total OTP submissions (3) so a genuinely wrong secret still aborts instead of looping forever. Scrape the message from BOTH markup shapes - <span id="input-error..."> and the kc-feedback-text banner - a regex matching only the first prints nothing on the OTP page. Shipped in scripts/postman/mint-code-flow-token.py.

description: The rig's 'in-network token caveat' is imprecise about WHAT is enforced, and the compose file's issuer pin is a no-op. (1) infra/compose.keycloak.yaml sets KC_HOSTNAME_URL=http://keycloak:8888 with a comment claiming it keeps the issuer stable - that option does NOT exist in Keycloak 26; with KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false the issuer is derived from the request's Host header. Measured 2026-08-14: a token minted through the host port 28888 carries iss=http://localhost:28888/realms/catalog-demo, not the in-network one. (2) But APISIX's openid-connect plugin (use_jwks=true) validates the SIGNATURE, not the issuer: that host-issuer token still reached a 200 through the gateway, while a token with one byte flipped in the signature 401'd. So 'the gateway rejects a host-minted token' is not what happens on this rig - the real reason every runner mints in-network is the browser/discovery flow, not iss enforcement.
resolution: For a HOST-SIDE scripted OIDC flow (the step-up code-flow miner), connect to localhost:28888 but send the IN-NETWORK authority as the Host header - the minted token then carries the same iss every in-network ROPC token does, with no container on the compose network. The flip side: every URL Keycloak renders (form actions, 302 Locations) then names keycloak:8888 and is unreachable from the host, so rebase each one onto the connect URL before following it (scheme://netloc swap, and match the redirect_uri BEFORE rebasing so the final code hop is not rewritten). Take parity by construction rather than trusting the validator's leniency, and keep an --issuer flag to opt out. Verify any 'the gateway accepted it' assertion with a TAMPERED-token control in the same run, or it proves nothing.

description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION layer-3 round 6. An issuer-allowlist pre-function added to APISIX's OIDC routes admitted keycloak:8888 (in-network) and localhost:28888 (published KC port) — and 401'd EVERY demo-SPA call. The SPA's authority is window.location.origin (example-demo-ui/src/auth.ts): its whole PKCE flow runs through the gateway's /realms/* passthrough, keycloak-pool sets no pass_host so APISIX forwards Host: localhost:9085, and Keycloak (KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false) rewrites its advertised issuer to that gateway origin. Vite dev is identical — the :3000 proxy sets changeOrigin:true, so the Host is still :9085. THE VALIDATION BLIND SPOT: every postman runner mints in-network, so the full suite (step-up 55/55, run-tests 22/22) stayed green while the browser path was dead. The regression was caught only by an adversarial review round that read auth.ts and reproduced it with curl -H 'Host: localhost:9085'.
resolution: There are THREE rig authorities, not two: keycloak:8888 (runners + miner + APISIX discovery), localhost:9085 (THE GATEWAY ORIGIN — the SPA, packaged and dev), localhost:28888 (published KC port). Any edge check keyed on iss/origin must admit all three; keep the list in one documented, overridable shell var. Pair every deny control with an ALLOW control in the e2e: a forged-Host 401 cell proves the guard bites, but only a gateway-Host 200 cell proves it does not bite the browser. General rule: when hardening an auth edge, enumerate the token-MINTING paths (not the token-USING paths) — an e2e suite that mints one way cannot see a break in another.

description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION layer-3 round 7. The issuer-allowlist serverless-pre-function extracted the token with auth:match('^[Bb]earer%s+(.+)') and returned (skipping the check) when it did not match. The openid-connect plugin it guards is case-INSENSITIVE: apisix/plugins/openid-connect.lua does string.lower(res[1]) == 'bearer', and resty/openidc.lua lowercases too. So the guard's SKIP set was strictly larger than the authenticator's REJECT set: an Authorization header spelling the scheme BEARER carried a foreign-issuer token past the issuer check AND authenticated, reaching the upstream on every guarded route (measured live; bEaReR too). The guard's own comment claimed it only narrows because a malformed bearer passes through to openid-connect which rejects it — false for exactly this input. GENERAL SHAPE: any belt-and-braces pre-check placed BESIDE an authenticator must be at least as permissive in what it INSPECTS as the authenticator is in what it ACCEPTS; the gap between the two parsers is the bypass.
resolution: Lowercase before matching (auth:lower():match('^bearer%s')) then slice with a scheme-agnostic pattern. Probe EVERY cased spelling in the e2e (Bearer, BEARER, bEaReR) and EVERY route the guard rides — a guard installed on three routes but probed on one is two-thirds unproven. Pin the JWT segment count exactly rather than a prefix match. Read the actual plugin source out of the running image (docker exec, cat the plugin lua) instead of assuming its parsing rules.
